title: Claims Training Notes: Sensor Recalibration Days on Larger-Class Partner Rentals
content:
These training notes cover recalibration days owed for driver-assistance sensors on accepted larger-class partner rentals under Cardinal Rental Reimbursement. The figures come from the estimate entries on the Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage claim.

**Rule.** Recalibration days are owed for driver-assistance sensors after supplemental damage, as follows:

- the claim carries a supplement estimate, and the latest estimate amount on the claim is $2000.00 or more: **2 days**;
- the claim carries a supplement estimate, and the latest estimate amount is $1000.00 or more but below $2000.00: **1 day**;
- otherwise: none.

## Questions answered

**What counts as a supplement estimate?**
An estimate on the physical damage claim with an estimate sequence of 1 or higher. The original estimate is sequence 0.

**Which amount is compared with the thresholds?**
The amount of the latest estimate written on the claim.

**Does a large original estimate earn recalibration days on its own?**
No. Without a supplement estimate on the claim, no recalibration days are owed, whatever the amount.

**What happens exactly at the thresholds?**
The thresholds include their own amount. At $2000.00 exactly, 2 days are owed. At $1000.00 exactly, 1 day is owed.

## Boundary table (hypothetical latest estimate amounts, supplement on the claim)

| Latest estimate amount | Recalibration days owed |
|---|---|
| $2000.00 | 2 |
| $1999.99 | 1 |
| $1000.00 | 1 |
| $999.99 | 0 |

With no supplement on the claim, a latest estimate of $3500.00 (hypothetical) gives 0 days.
